chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“ʿAlī عليه السلام did not hold ghusl to be required for anything except the greater fluid.”

This report indicates the obligation of ghusl from the greater fluid, whether it is discharged with desire or without desire, whether that occurs in sleep or in wakefulness, and in every condition. And his statement, “he did not hold ghusl to be required except for the greater fluid,” means that if the two circumcised parts have not met, then after that there is no ghusl for anything except the greater fluid, as indicated by the earlier reports.

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports used as supporting evidence
key_terms.الْخِتَانَانِ: the two circumcised parts, referring to sexual intercourse
key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: ritual bath required for major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْأَكْبَرِ: the greater fluid that necessitates ghusl

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This text states that ghusl becomes obligatory due to the discharge of the greater fluid, regardless of whether it occurs with desire or without desire, in sleep or while awake. It also clarifies that where there has been no meeting of the two circumcised parts, ghusl is not required for anything else besides the greater fluid.
